title: Dimension of a Physical Quantity
notes:
Definition

The dimension of a physical quantity is the power to which the fundamental quantities are raised in its expression. It tells us how the quantity depends on mass, length and time.

Dimensions are written in square brackets in the form [MᵃLᵇTᶜ]. The dimension of force, for example, is [M¹L¹T⁻²] — read as "mass to power 1, length to power 1, time to power −2". It is often written in short as (1, 1, −2).

Dimensions of Common Quantities

QuantityFormulaDimension
Force$F = ma$[M¹L¹T⁻²]
Area$A = l^2$[M⁰L²T⁰]
Density$\rho = m/V$[M¹L⁻³T⁰]
Velocity$v = s/t$[M⁰L¹T⁻¹]
Acceleration$a = v/t$[M⁰L¹T⁻²]
Work / Energy$W = Fd$[M¹L²T⁻²]
Power$P = W/t$[M¹L²T⁻³]
Momentum$p = mv$[M¹L¹T⁻¹]
Frequency$f = 1/T$[M⁰L⁰T⁻¹]
Angle (sin θ)ratio of two lengths[M⁰L⁰T⁰] — dimensionless

Why Dimensions Matter

Dimensional analysis is one of the most useful tools in physics:

  • Checking correctness — the principle of homogeneity verifies whether an equation is dimensionally right.
  • Unit conversion — converting a value from one system of units to another (for example, joule to erg).
  • Deriving relations — building a formula when the quantities involved are known.
  • Finding constants — determining the dimension of unknown constants inside equations.
examples:
**Q1: Define dimension of a physical quantity.**

**Answer:** The power raised to the fundamental quantities in its expression.

**Q2: What is the dimension of force?**

**Answer:** [M1L1T-2].

**Q3: What is the dimension of area?**

**Answer:** [M0L2T0].

**Q4: What is the dimension of density?**

**Answer:** [M1L-3T0].

**Q5: What is the dimension of velocity?**

**Answer:** [M0L1T-1].

**Q6: What is the dimension of acceleration?**

**Answer:** [M0L1T-2].

**Q7: What is the dimension of work?**

**Answer:** [M1L2T-2].

**Q8: What is the dimension of power?**

**Answer:** [M1L2T-3].

**Q9: What is the dimension of momentum?**

**Answer:** [M1L1T-1].

**Q10: What is the dimension of frequency?**

**Answer:** [M0L0T-1].

**Q11: What is dimensional formula written in?**

**Answer:** Square brackets, e.g. [M1L2T-2].

**Q12: Why is dimension analysis useful?**

**Answer:** It helps check correctness of equations, convert units, and derive relations.

**Q13: What is the dimension of a dimensionless quantity like angle?**

**Answer:** [M0L0T0].

**Q14: What is the dimension of gravitational constant G?**

**Answer:** [M-1L3T-2].

**Q15: What is the dimension of gas constant R?**

**Answer:** [M1L2T-2mol-1K-1].

**Q16: How many fundamental dimensions does mechanics typically use?**

**Answer:** Three — M, L, and T.

**Q17: What is the dimension of pressure?**

**Answer:** [M1L-1T-2].

**Q18: What is the dimension of latent heat?**

**Answer:** [L2T-2].

**Q19: What is the dimension of specific heat capacity?**

**Answer:** [L2T-2K-1].

**Q20: What is the dimensional formula of time period?**

**Answer:** [M0L0T1].

**Q21: How do you find the dimension of a derived quantity from its formula?**

**Answer:** Substitute the dimensions of its component quantities and simplify using powers.

**Q22: Why does sinθ have zero dimension?**

**Answer:** Because it is a ratio of two lengths (perpendicular/hypotenuse).

**Q23: State the dimensional formula of mass.**

**Answer:** [M1L0T0].

**Q24: State the dimensional formula of length.**

**Answer:** [M0L1T0].

**Q25: State the dimensional formula of time.**

**Answer:** [M0L0T1].

**Q26: What principle states LHS and RHS must have same dimension?**

**Answer:** The principle of homogeneity of dimensions.
keyPoints: - **Definition:** The dimension of a physical quantity is the power raised to the fundamental quantities in its expression.
summary: The dimension of a physical quantity is the power raised to the fundamental quantities in its expression. Key examples include Dimension of Force = (1,1,-2) i.e. [M1L1T-2]; Dimension of Area = (0,2,0) i.e. [M0L2T0]; Dimension of Density = (1,-3,0) i.e. [M1L-3T0].
